# 1.2.78 - a player's actions and rolls reach the GM again, and the first drag into a new room counts

Two fixes released on their own, ahead of the next stage of the plan.

On 1.2.77 at a Foundry v14 table on The Forge, with a GM connected, a
player could not act: an action from the grid said "That action could not
be completed. Tell the GM." and a statistic clicked on the sheet rolled
nothing. The player's console named the cause: the module's wait for the
GM's answer started its timer in a way a browser refuses. It was so from
1.2.62 on, for every request a player's client waits on; the test harness
runs outside a browser and never saw it. Its timers now refuse the same
way.

The second fix (stage E84):
On 1.2.77 at a Foundry v14 table, the GM's Monokuma dragged into another
room kept the old room on the room tile (its name, description and
picture), played no arrival in the fog and was not announced as a move
into the new room until a second drag inside it. A player's character
may have missed its crossing the same way; that was not seen at the
table. The module now reads the token's room once more when it comes to
rest, so the first drag counts. In the plan, the secret passages stage
(E79) moves to 1.2.79; in `tools/stages.json` the planned stages after
this one move up one number, all but the last (1.3.0).

## At the table

- **A player's action and a statistic clicked on the sheet** reach the GM
  again: every request a player's client waits on is sent and its answer
  waited for, as the module meant from 1.2.62. This is measured in the
  headless harness only (scenario 33 and the suite, below), not yet at a
  table (LIVE-E84-01).
- **A drag into another room** shows the new room on the room tile, plays
  the fog's arrival and, for a player's character, is charged once, on
  the first drag. The fog follows about a third of a second after the
  token stops; the tile and the charge the same, or a second and a half
  later when the hook read only a step of the drag. However long Foundry
  reports the token as moving, the second reading starts at most about
  five seconds after the hook's own reading ends (the fog's, at most
  about three and a half seconds after the update). The tile and the
  charge are
  measured in the headless harness (scenario 74, phase L); the timings
  and the fog's arrival, which needs a canvas, are read in the code
  only. At a table all of it is LIVE-E78-14.
- **A drag that the hook already read where it ended** works as before:
  the second reading finds the room already recorded and does nothing.
  The scenarios' drags are such drags, and they stay green (scenarios
  66 and 40, the suite; every scenario check by check against the run
  on 1.2.77's tree, in Checked).
- **With the module's debug on**, the console of the browser that read a
  move again says "read again at rest", with the room it had recorded and
  the room the token stands in. It also says so when a step of the drag
  was still noted, whatever the room. At a table that line tells which
  drags needed the second reading.

## Changed

- **`scripts/bridge-guards.mjs`**: the wait for the GM's answer starts and
  clears its timers by calling the browser's own `setTimeout` and
  `clearTimeout` as functions (`WINDOW_CLOCK`). Until now it called them as
  methods of another object, which a browser refuses ("'setTimeout' called
  on an object that does not implement interface Window." in Firefox), so
  the request threw before it was sent.
- **The test harness** (`audit/harness/client-entry.mjs`): a client's
  timers, `fetch`, `queueMicrotask` and `structuredClone` refuse any
  receiver but the window, as a browser's do. With only this change on
  1.2.77's code, scenario 33 fails with the error the owner's console
  showed, through the same three lines of the wait, for another request.
- **Two tests**: R570 (tier 1) builds the wait as the module does, with no
  clock of its own, and sends, answers and times out a request on it;
  R571 (tier 0) reads every file of the module for one of those browser
  functions taken as a value instead of called, and finds none (on
  1.2.77's code it finds the two in the wait).
- **`scripts/movement.mjs`**: a character's move is judged once more where
  the token stands, after its movement animation and any pending movement
  are over (at most 3 s, then 250 ms). It runs only for a character whose
  room this browser has recorded, when no newer move of that token arrived
  meanwhile, no put-back is on its way, no route of it is still being
  settled, and the room differs from the one recorded or a pending step of
  the drag is still noted (then after a further 1.5 s of quiet). The move
  is then judged and announced again (`drpgRouteSettled`, which the room
  tile repaints on), naming the room the token stands in; a crossing is
  charged once.
- **`scripts/fog.mjs`**: the fog's local repaint and the primary GM's
  discovery ledger also run once more at rest; both change nothing when
  the room is the one already read.
- **Scenario 74** has a new phase, L, that stands in two readings that
  could explain the report, on the browser that judges the move, by
  holding the token's position and movement state on its document: the
  GM's Monokuma from the Hall to the Cafeteria and a player's character
  into a new room with the hook reading the drag's start, and the same
  character back by a last update that still has a step pending.
- **The audit's live checks** gain item 236 (LIVE-E78-14).
- **`tools/stages.json`** carries E84 as 1.2.78 and moves every later
  planned stage but 1.3.0 one number on.
- **The manifest's compatibility and relationships are unchanged**:
  Daggerheart `minimum` and `verified` stay 2.6.5, Foundry `verified`
  stays 14.365.

## Known gaps

- Why players' rolls worked at this table before is not known: the cause
  is in every version from 1.2.62. Not measured.
- The fix is measured only in the headless harness, whose timers now
  refuse as Firefox and Chromium are documented to; it was not run in a
  real browser at a table (LIVE-E84-01).
- Which of the two readings happened at the owner's table is not
  measured. The fix covers both, but neither was seen on a real Foundry v14
  (LIVE-E78-14).
- A player's character was not seen to miss a crossing at the table. In
  the harness it goes through the same second reading as the GM's
  Monokuma, but is judged as a student: its crossing is charged, the
  Monokuma's never is.
- When the hook read the drag's start, the move is announced twice: first
  for the room the token left, then at rest for the room it stands in.
  Only the room tile listens, and it draws the room it is told, so the
  tile ends on the right room (read in the code and in phase L).
- The fog's second reading is not measured: the harness draws no canvas,
  so scenario 74 reads the tile, the charge and the announcement only.
- When Foundry reports a token as moving for longer than three seconds,
  the second reading does not wait longer: it reads the token where it is
  then (read in the code).

## Checked

- The full test run (`npm test`) on the tree with both fixes, commit
  d69801d: green, in 77 min 53 s (78 min 15 s with the wait for the
  machine's locks). It is compared with the full run on the E84 fix's
  tree (commit 7ac773b, below). The suite (1340 passed, 0 failed, 23
  skipped) is test by test the same, in the same order and with the same
  reasons, but for the two new tests, R570 and R571. The 26 scenarios
  are green, each with the same checks (scenario 33 45 of 45, scenario 74
  41 of 41). Scenarios 72 and 75 keep the expected reds they had (three
  and one).
- The wait's fix, shown red first: with only the harness's new timers on
  1.2.77's code, scenario 33 fails with "Could not send ... to the GM
  TypeError: 'setTimeout' called on an object that does not implement
  interface Window.", thrown at bridge-guards.mjs line 1712 by way of
  lines 1677 and 1820, the three lines the owner's console named. With the
  fix, scenario 33 is 45 of 45 with no such error, and the lint, the
  checks (13 parts) and the gate's self-test (36 of 36) are green.
- R571's reading, run as a script over the module's files: on 1.2.77's
  code it names two, `setTimeout` and `clearTimeout` taken as values in
  the wait's default clock; on this tree none, of 134 files. R570 was not
  run on 1.2.77's code.
- The full test run on the E84 fix's tree, commit 7ac773b: green, in 78
  min 44 s (79 min 38 s with the wait for the machine's locks). It is
  compared with the full run on 1.2.77's tree before its release commit
  (3ad0ca0). The suite (1338 passed, 0 failed, 23 skipped) is test by
  test the same, in the same order and with the same reasons. The 26
  scenarios are green, each with the same checks but scenario 74, which
  gains phase L's three (41 of 41, where it had 38 of 38).
- Scenario 74 alone, on the E84 fix's tree: 41 of 41 checks in 81.9 s.
  With the fix taken out, phase L's three checks fail: L1 and L2 with the
  tile on the old room, L2 and L3 with no action charged. L3 ran after L2
  had failed, so the pending-step reading was not shown failing on its
  own. Scenarios 66 (62 of 62) and 40 (86 of 86) green on the same tree.
- The ledger row: on copies with module.json at 1.2.78, `ship E84` is
  refused on 1.2.77's ledger and `check` fails; on this one `ship E84`
  writes 1.2.78 and `check` passes.
- The ledger commit 87b963e changes `tools/stages.json` and a comment in
  `tools/stages.mjs` only; the full run was not repeated on it alone, and
  the full run on d69801d includes it.
- The E84 fix is commit 7ac773b, the ledger row 87b963e and the wait's
  fix d69801d. None of the three had a review of its code by a second
  reader; these notes were read against the code and the logs.
- Not checked in a real Foundry yet: the audit's live checks, section
  9.2, items 236 (LIVE-E78-14) and 237 (LIVE-E84-01), and the earlier
  ones the 1.2.77 notes name. The local release gate needs a local
  Foundry v14 and did not run for this release.
